title: Bounded register-program scan
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, let $y$ be a Boolean word of positive length, let $R$ be a register assignment, and let $p$ be a natural number. Write $B=(8W+8)(|y|+1)$, where $W$ is the chunk width determined by $N$. Suppose every register of $R$ is at most $B$, $R_L=|y|$, $R_P=p\le |y|$, and $R_{Q1}=R_{Cap}=R_{Q2}=R_S=R_T=0$. Then either the suffix $y[p:]$ has canonical form (every nonempty such word ends in $1$) and length at most the binary expansion length of $|y|$, and there are $q_1,cap\le B$ such that the codec program in the chosen mode reaches its next designated state with $Q1=q_1$, $Cap=cap$, $Q2=p$, and $S$ equal to the binary value of $y[p:]$, while satisfying its guard; or that suffix condition fails and the program halts with answer false while satisfying its guard throughout.
hypotheses_covered: N is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine
mode is one of the codec modes
Every register of R is at most (8W+8)(|y|+1)
caveat: The reachability and guard predicates depend on detailed register-program semantics; this paraphrase states the register changes, bound, and failure behavior, but does not expand those definitions.
